standard.title: Practise safe and expressive movement
standard.description: experiment with and practise skills for moving safely and expressively using fundamental movement skills and the elements of dance
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can move safely and expressively using fundamental movement skills and elements of dance (Y1-2). They have established spatial awareness and can use movement quality to communicate ideas.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with and practise skills for moving safely and expressively using fundamental movement skills and the elements of dance.

nodes.label: Safe practice as habit
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate safe dance practice as a consistent habit — including warm-up and cool-down, and surface/footwear awareness.
nodes.minimum_width: Independently warming up before dance activity and cooling down after; removing socks on slippery surfaces; demonstrating spatial awareness consistently across sessions.
nodes.typical_width: Developing the habit of safe dance practice: warming up before complex movement patterns; cooling/calming down afterwards; adapting to surface conditions; maintaining spatial awareness and body control as complexity increases.
wider: Lead a warm-up sequence for a small group — making decisions about what to include and why
Reflect explicitly on how warm-up changes movement capacity — comparing quality of movement before and after
nodes.hinge_reason: Safe practice at this band involves students taking increased personal responsibility — not just following instructions. This self-regulatory habit is necessary before students can engage with more complex technical demands (balance, coordination, accuracy) without injury risk.

response_modes.reason: Safe practice must be fully habitual before technical complexity increases. Consistent reinforcement across sessions — not one-off instruction — builds the automatic self-regulation this requires.

success_criteria: Student independently initiates warm-up before dance activity
Student makes at least one independent safe practice decision during a session (e.g. adjusts footwear, identifies space)

nodes.label: Technical skills — body control and accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can refine technical movement skills — body control, accuracy, alignment, strength, balance and coordination — in fundamental movements.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrating body control and accuracy in at least two fundamental movement types in response to teacher feedback.
nodes.typical_width: Developing body awareness and refining technical skills in fundamental movements: control, accuracy, alignment, strength, balance, coordination; exploring known movements to find alternative ways of performing them (waving at different levels, with different body parts, bigger/smaller); using contrast and repetition to explore and generate new movement.
wider: Focus sustained technical practice on one complex movement type (e.g. rolling, jumping and landing, balance sequences) — refining quality across multiple attempts
Explore how the same technical skill (e.g. balance) can be used expressively — comparing technical execution with expressive intent

response_modes.reason: Technical precision requires repeated practice with feedback. Set specific technical targets and return to them across sessions — accuracy, alignment and balance are skills that improve with deliberate repetition, not one-off exposure.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who develop technical precision across a range of fundamental movements build a physical toolkit that enables genuine expressive choice — expressiveness without technical control is limited.
success_criteria: Student demonstrates improved body control or accuracy in a target movement following teacher feedback
Student can perform a fundamental movement with attention to at least two technical qualities (e.g. alignment and balance)

nodes.label: Using elements to communicate ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use the elements of dance deliberately to communicate ideas — connecting physical skill to expressive intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Using at least two elements intentionally in a movement sequence to communicate a specific idea.
nodes.typical_width: Exploring how elements of dance communicate ideas: using elements to develop locomotor and non-locomotor movements representing aspects of a story (character walks, emotions, moods of a place); making deliberate element choices to express ideas clearly.
wider: Explore how cultural stories can be shared through dance — using element choices to represent different aspects of a specific cultural narrative
Compare how changing one element (e.g. switching from slow to sharp dynamics) changes what an idea communicates — developing selective expressive awareness

response_modes.reason: Communicative movement integrates technical skill (N2) with element awareness and intent. This is where physical capacity becomes expressive capacity — connect technical work explicitly to expressive purpose.

success_criteria: Student uses at least two elements intentionally in movement — can explain the expressive purpose of each choice
An observer can identify what idea the student is communicating from their movement quality
